headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad tool access create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure between Continue and semantica.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP; semantica also reads/writes files and exposes MCP resources. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs from the shared filesystem or MCP channel. The pairwise pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP resource namespace
IF either agent parses the other's file output as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP on one side for the shared task
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent files
Add a manual review step before executing any generated instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers, while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and secrets. Because both can read/write files and semantica can ingest many local and remote sources, a shared workspace can move sensitive data from semantica into Continue's editor context or outputs. The blast radius includes secrets and regulated documents.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or synced workspace
IF semantica ingests documents containing secrets or regulated records into the shared graph
mitigations: Use separate repositories or directories
Redact secrets before semantica ingestion
Restrict Continue to non-sensitive files only
Turn off shared filesystem sync between agents
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, subprocess spawning, package installation, and MCP access; semantica also modifies git state. In a shared directory or repo, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt git and generated artifacts. The overlap is explicit in both profiles and dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or repository
IF semantica performs git operations while Continue writes workspace files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent
Run one agent in read-only mode for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can emit code or edits from editor context, and semantica can build decision records, provenance, and downstream artifacts from ingested inputs. If semantica treats Continue's output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into structured records, contracts, or audit trails. Both profiles support the pathway, and no default verification barrier is stated.
conditions: IF semantica ingests Continue-generated files or text without validation
IF downstream artifacts are produced from those inputs
mitigations: Require human review before semantica commits records
Add schema validation on all Continue outputs
Mark Continue outputs as untrusted provenance
Compare outputs against source files before ingestion
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in the orchestrator

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE assistant handling source code and editor buffers, while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and secrets. If regulated or confidential data is placed into the shared pair, semantica's broader ingestion and OAuth/M2M surfaces can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated data such as contracts, audit trails, or secrets is processed by both agents
IF the deployment requires a specific residency, retention, or subject-rights policy not documented in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workflow
Review retention settings for both agents
Restrict semantica to approved data classes only
Document a DPA and residency boundary before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
